concepts.label: Minority erasure
concepts.definition: Removal, flattening, misclassification, de-authoring, or invisibilisation of a marginalised, under-represented, or structurally disadvantaged person or group in a record, system, summary, dataset, policy process, or public narrative.

concepts.label: Authorship erasure
concepts.definition: Loss, misattribution, replacement, or weakening of the original author's role, authority, or contribution.

concepts.label: Context erasure
concepts.definition: Removal of social, cultural, historical, disability, access, language, geographic, or power context that materially affects meaning.

concepts.label: Consent erasure
concepts.definition: Reuse of material outside the recorded consent scope, purpose, audience, format, timing, or withdrawal conditions.

concepts.label: Accessibility erasure
concepts.definition: Omission or downgrading of required communication and access supports.

concepts.label: Metadata erasure
concepts.definition: Failure to preserve authorship, provenance, permissions, access needs, version history, review state, or withdrawal terms in durable metadata.

concepts.label: Translation erasure
concepts.definition: Representation through another speaker, institution, summariser, or AI system in a way that changes authority, tone, meaning, uncertainty, or lived-experience significance.

concepts.label: Institutional reframing
concepts.definition: Rewriting lived experience to protect, promote, simplify, or legitimise an organisation instead of preserving the author's meaning and authority.

review_rules.then: mark erasure_risk as high and require human review

review_rules.if: record.ai_use.summary_generated is true and record.human_review.completed is false
record.accessibility.required_formats contains items not present in record.publication.formats
